title: The Ember Compass
description: A lost artifact. An ancient forest. Three adventurers who may not survive the night. Follow the trail of a legendary compass said to guide its bearer through any darkness — but darkness has teeth.

scenarios.label: Attack it
scenarios.prompt: Draw your weapon and attack the Hollow One before it can act.

scenarios.label: Shadowstep
scenarios.prompt: Use your shadowstepping ability to vanish and flank the creature.

scenarios.label: Talk to it
scenarios.prompt: Hold your ground and demand to know what the Hollow One is and what it wants.

scenarios.label: Ask Sylvara
scenarios.prompt: Ask Sylvara what she can sense about the creature's nature — magic, undead, something else?

scenarios.label: Scout ahead
scenarios.prompt: Break away from the group and push deeper into the forest, following the trail toward the Ember Compass.

scenarios.label: Search the area
scenarios.prompt: Scan the surrounding undergrowth and treeline for clues — tracks, markings, anything that might point toward the compass.

scenarios.label: Fall back
scenarios.prompt: Signal the party to retreat toward the forest edge and regroup.

scenarios.label: Find Mira
scenarios.prompt: Head back to the village and press Mira for everything she knows about the Hollow One and the compass.

setup.label: Describe your character (follows "You are")
setup.default: a seasoned ranger, lean and sharp-eyed, with sun-darkened skin and a quiet intensity that unsettles strangers.

setup.label: What powers do you have? (follows "You have")
setup.default: a ranger's keen instincts and a gift for shadowstepping — vanishing from sight for a few seconds when you need it most.

npcs.name: Mira
npcs.note: Knows local rumours. Owes a favour.

npcs.name: The Hollow One
npcs.note: Encountered in the forest. Motives unclear.

entries.text: The ancient forest of Mirefall stretches endlessly before you, its gnarled canopy blotting out the noon sun. You arrived here following rumours of a lost artifact — the Ember Compass — said to guide its bearer through any darkness.

Gorvath cracks his knuckles beside you, his armour catching what little light filters through the leaves. Sylvara floats a pale magelight orb overhead, her eyes scanning the tree line with quiet unease.
You keep your voice low. "Something moved behind that oak. I've been tracking it for the last ten minutes — it's not an animal."

Sylvara's orb flickers. A low, rhythmic clicking sound rises from the undergrowth, as if a dozen bones are tapping against each other. Gorvath draws his broadsword with a slow, deliberate scrape of steel.
You nock an arrow and step silently toward the oak, eyes narrowing as you peer into the shadows.

From the darkness emerges a creature — half man, half shadow — its form rippling at the edges like smoke in wind. It raises one elongated hand and speaks in a voice that sounds like crumpling parchment.
